questions.question_text: Which is the standard expanded form of $308\,040\,506$?

options.why: Placed the $4$ in the hundred-thousands place instead of the ten-thousands place.
Gave the $8$ a ten-millions value instead of its actual millions value.
Placed the $5$ in the tens column instead of the hundreds column.
Placed $700\,000$ as $70\,000$, shifting the $7$ one column to the right.
Placed the $30$ in the hundreds column and the $9$ in ones, creating $309$ instead of $039$.
Swapped the $60$ million and $2$ million contributions when forming the millions period.

questions.question_text: How many thousands are equal to $1$ million?

options.why: Used only two place-value steps, giving $100\times1\,000=100\,000$ rather than one million.
Used four place-value steps, giving ten million rather than one million.
Repeated the number of ones in a million instead of counting groups of one thousand.

questions.question_text: How many millions are equal to $1$ billion?

options.why: Counted only to one hundred million, which is one tenth of a billion.
Counted ten thousand millions, which makes ten billion rather than one billion.
Used the number of ones in a million instead of the number of million-sized groups in a billion.

questions.question_text: Rename $9\,600\,000$ as a number of hundred-thousands.

options.why: Counted ten times too many groups, as if each group were worth only $10\,000$.
Divided by one million instead of by one hundred thousand.
Counted groups of one thousand rather than groups of one hundred thousand.
Subtracted the final $650$ from $1\,000$ instead of finding the full difference from $270\,000$.
Removed only $230\,000$ from the original number instead of the stated $270\,000$.
Subtracted $270$ rather than $270\,000$, ignoring the unit size of the first part.

questions.question_text: A warehouse has $7\,350\,000$ bolts packed in lots of $10\,000$. How many lots are represented?

options.why: Counted thousand-sized lots, producing ten times as many lots as the stated $10\,000$ size.
Counted hundred-thousand-sized lots instead of lots of ten thousand.
Counted groups of one hundred rather than the required groups of ten thousand.

questions.question_text: An inventory is written as $62$ hundred-thousands $+45$ thousands $+19$ ones. Which numeral represents it?

options.why: Treated $62$ hundred-thousands as $62$ million instead of $6.2$ million.
Placed $45$ thousands as $4\,500$ and merged it into the final period.
Rounded $45$ thousands to $50$ thousands instead of preserving the exact regrouped amount.
